版本/迁移矩阵 -- configuration and schema evolution have a version and
This file is that matrix. It did not exist: the checker printed two
version numbers and then a prose line describing 'the acceptance
matrix', which was a description of nothing. An audit of these
Each row is one versioned interface: where its version lives, what
this build produces, what it accepts, and what happens to an artifact
or a peer that is outside that range. 'refuse' is a verdict, not a
failure to try: every one of them is a named error code a caller can

interfaces.older: refuse, code ARTIFACT_INVALID. No migration is offered: there has been no earlier released format, so a 0.x artifact would be something this project never produced.
interfaces.newer: refuse, code ARTIFACT_INVALID. A newer container may describe segments this loader cannot place, and guessing is how a loader hands a device the wrong bytes.
interfaces.tested_by: R36-CFG-03, which edits the header to format 99 and requires the refusal

interfaces.what: the argument ABI a kernel's parameters are laid out by
interfaces.newer: refuse, code ABI_MISMATCH -- including a higher MINOR. A minor bump may add a parameter kind the runtime cannot lay out, and accepting it because the major matched would place arguments by guess.
interfaces.tested_by: R36-CFG-03's ABI-VERSION case: accepts 1.0, refuses 1.1 and 2.0

interfaces.version_lives_in: spec/r2_transport_v1.json, and the file name carries the version
interfaces.newer: a device speaking a later protocol would answer the v1 mailbox with fields this host does not read. The file name is the version, so a second protocol is a second file and a second binding.
interfaces.tested_by: R36-IO-01, which drives every operation of v1

interfaces.newer: refuse at `hello`. The handshake is before any device work, so a mismatch costs nothing.
interfaces.tested_by: R36-TEST-01 CONF-LIFE opens the backend, which performs the handshake

interfaces.what: the configuration an artifact was compiled for
interfaces.version_lives_in: config_hash in the artifact manifest, computed by tnca.profiles.config_hash
interfaces.produces: a hash of the profile, elaboration, core count, topology and capabilities
interfaces.accepts: an exact match with the session's profile
interfaces.older: refuse, code PROFILE_MISMATCH, before any device request. There is no migration: a different configuration is a different machine.
interfaces.tested_by: R36-CFG-02, which loads a core-sim artifact on core-vrf-sync-v1 and requires zero device requests

interfaces.version_lives_in: the cache key, which contains the toolchain lock hash and the config hash
interfaces.produces: one entry per (source, signature, constexprs, semantic options, profile, lock)
interfaces.older: an entry for another implementation simply does not match, so it cannot be served. This is the 'cache 不跨不兼容实现命中' requirement and it is structural rather than checked at read time.
interfaces.tested_by: R36-CFG-01, which shows the same source on two profiles produces two keys and two config hashes

interfaces.accepts: consumers read the format field before anything else
interfaces.newer: a consumer that does not recognise the format must stop rather than read the file lists.
interfaces.tested_by: R36-RTL-01, which requires the manifest's fields including the format

interfaces.what: tnca.backend.Backend, the interface a platform implements
interfaces.version_lives_in: the class itself; there is no number
interfaces.accepts: a subclass that implements all of them; Python refuses to instantiate one that does not
interfaces.older: a binding written against a smaller interface fails to instantiate, loudly, at registration.
interfaces.newer: adding a method is breaking for every existing binding. It has happened once, `ping`, and doc/r36_handoff.md section 8 records it.
interfaces.tested_by: R36-TEST-01, which runs the same suite against every registered backend

migration_policy: Nothing in this table migrates. Every mismatch is refused with a
named code, before any device work.
That is a decision, not an omission. A migration path is a second
implementation of a format, and the two drift; refusing costs a
recompile, which is cheap here because compiling is seconds and the
cache makes the second one free. When a released artifact is
expensive enough to be worth migrating, this table is where the path
gets written down and R36-CFG-03 is where it gets a test.
